closures.observed_problem: Seven of the eight authenticated account route trees rendered for any authenticated merchant-side user. A Personnel user could render the Finance, Branch, HR, Front Office, Audit or Merchant Administrator shell.
closures.evidence: /merchant, /branch, /hr, /finance, /front-office, /personnel and /audit each carried `beforeEnter: [requiresAuth, requiresActiveMerchant]`. Only /platform carried `requiresAccount`, added by UI-03 to close UI01-ROLE-001.
closures.root_cause: UI-03 closed UI01-ROLE-001 for the /platform tree only and deferred the remaining seven to UI-07. Those trees kept `requiresAuth` (is anyone signed in?) and `requiresActiveMerchant` (is the merchant active?), neither of which takes an account as input.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: `requiresActiveMerchant` has no account parameter, so it cannot distinguish Finance from Personnel. No amount of correct behaviour elsewhere could have prevented the wrong shell rendering.
closures.correct_fix: Attach the existing `requiresAccount(<account>)` to each tree root — the same guard, unchanged, that UI-03 proved — and declare `meta.accountKey` on the root so the requirement is readable from the router record. The guard still requires the route's account, the SERVER-resolved host account and an account the user actually holds to agree, and still fails closed on any disagreement.
closures.why_meta_was_added: `requiresAccount(...)` returns an anonymous closure, so a coverage test inspecting `beforeEnter` can only see an unnamed function. It would have passed vacuously on an unguarded tree — which is exactly the failure being closed.

closures.observed_problem: Four contract pages were exposed as live routes that implemented nothing: /platform/dashboard, /front-office/dashboard, /personnel/dashboard and /audit/dashboard returned 200 and rendered a page-shaped placeholder.
closures.evidence: All four resolved to `DashboardStub.vue`, a six-line component whose entire body reads "DashboardStub — Phase 4 stub — implementation in later phases". The screen inventory recorded all four as `implemented`, so nothing contradicted the claim.
closures.root_cause: Phase 4 scaffolded one placeholder per account shell so the route tree could be exercised before the pages existed. No later phase removed them, and the inventory's `implemented` status made the placeholder indistinguishable from a delivered screen.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The component has no data, no API call and no authorization. UI/UX plan §7.2 requires a planned page to create no dead or fake link, and §13.5 forbids satisfying the page count with a placeholder component — this is precisely that.
closures.correct_fix: Remove the four routes and the four now-dead components. The canonical contract reserves each page's route identity with `implementation_status: planned`, so the owner phase cannot silently rename it, and no runtime route or navigation link exists until that phase supplies a real component, read model, authorization, tests and browser proof.

closures.observed_problem: The first pass of the account guard denied a Merchant Administrator the branch list, branch creation, the branch record, its operating hours and staff invitations — five screens that account genuinely owns.
closures.evidence: docs/frontend/screens/inventory.json records branch-list, branch-detail and branch-operating-hours as BOTH merchant_administrator and merchant_branch, and branch-create as merchant_administrator ONLY. resources/spa/src/pages/hr/StaffInvitations.vue branches on auth.isMerchantAdmin() to offer Branch Manager / Human Resource to one account and the operational roles to the other. Five browser cases that had always passed began failing.
closures.root_cause: `/branch` and `/hr` were guarded as whole trees using the account implied by the PATH PREFIX. A path prefix is not an account boundary.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: Plan §13 assigns branch creation to the Merchant Administrator and explicitly denies it to the Branch Manager. Guarding `/branch` as `merchant_branch` therefore denied the account that owns the capability and left it reachable only by the account the Plan forbids. The failing tests encoded the Plan correctly; the guard encoded the URL.
closures.correct_fix: `requiresAccount(...accountKeys)` accepts the accounts that genuinely own a route. The tree root admits both owners; the ten Branch-only and nine HR-only children re-assert their single owner on their own records. The served host account must be one of the owners AND the user must hold THAT account, so host and held account still have to agree and nothing was widened beyond real ownership.
closures.what_was_not_done: No test was re-pointed to a different account to make it pass — doing so would have fabricated an authority Plan §13 denies. No route alias, wildcard account, all-accounts test user or environment bypass was added.
